log.msg: METHOD: lost.jsonl citations cite one or two transcript lines per file, but citation line numbers are NOT consistent -- a Read citation points at the tool_RESULT line (0-indexed array position used directly), while an Edit/Write citation points at the tool_USE line itself. Found by hand-checking two citations against their transcripts before writing any extractor.

BUG FOUND in the manifest itself: several yes entries cite a Read that is actually PARTIAL (an explicit offset/limit, e.g. public/app.js cited at only lines 1-40, public/styles.css at 1-45, public/framework/core/Page/words.js at an offset:108 limit:10 snippet) but were graded recoverable:yes as if the read were the whole file. Built the extractor to verify every Read for offset/limit before trusting it as a base, and to keep searching the WHOLE transcript corpus (not just the cited line) for a genuine full read when the cited one turns out partial.

BUG FOUND: a caching feature returns literal text "Wasted call - file unchanged since your last Read..." instead of real content on a repeat Read; my first pass mis-flagged that message itself as a valid full read (it has no offset/limit key) and then failed to strip it as file content. Fixed by excluding any Read whose result starts with "Wasted call".

DESIGN: to catch both manifest errors above, built one GLOBAL, timestamped index of every Read/Write/Edit/MultiEdit tool call across all 5 session transcripts on this machine (d6699955, cfca18c9, and three short fixture/utility sessions), not just the transcript(s) a lost.jsonl line happened to cite. For each of the 216 files, replayed every matching event up to that entry own cited final timestamp, in true chronological order, restarting from the freshest full Read/Write whenever an edit failed to apply against the current text (an append-only file like an improvements.md log genuinely gets edited by many unrelated agents on different days, so an early edit chain can legitimately go stale before a later, fully-authoritative Read of the same file). Only entries where a real, complete Read or Write is found ANYWHERE in that whole timeline, with every following edit applying cleanly, are called extracted; everything else is downgraded to partial rather than guessed.
